settings.name: Top notes
settings.text: Light, quick notes that greet you on spraying, then fade. They're why a perfume smells so bright on the test strip.

settings.name: Heart notes
settings.when: From about 15 minutes, for a few hours
settings.text: The character of the perfume once it settles: florals, spices and fruit. This is what people around you notice most.

settings.name: Base notes
settings.text: Rich, slow notes that anchor everything and stay longest on skin and clothes: the dry-down.
How long you can still smell it on your own skin.
How far the scent reaches from you in the first hours: close to the skin, or across a room.
The trail you leave behind when you walk past. French for the wake of a boat.
How a perfume smells once the top notes are gone: the part you live with all day.
A few notes blended so they read as one new smell, like a chord in music.
Why the same perfume smells a little different on you than on a friend.

settings.name: Citrus
settings.text: Zesty, sunny and quick to lift a mood.

settings.name: Fresh
settings.text: Clean, airy and green, like cool water or crushed leaves.

settings.name: Aromatic
settings.text: Herbs like lavender and sage: crisp and classic.

settings.name: Floral
settings.text: Petals and blossoms, from soft and powdery to bold.

settings.name: Spicy
settings.text: Pepper, cinnamon and cardamom: warm and lively.

settings.name: Gourmand
settings.text: Sweet and edible: vanilla, tonka, caramel.

settings.name: Amber
settings.text: Resins and warmth that glow on skin.

settings.name: Woody
settings.text: Cedar, vetiver and sandalwood: dry and grounding.

settings.title: Moisturise first
settings.text: Perfume holds on longer to hydrated skin; an unscented lotion helps.

settings.title: Spray, don't rub
settings.text: Rubbing your wrists together warms and breaks up the top notes.

settings.title: Aim for pulse points
settings.text: Neck, inner elbows and behind the knees warm the scent gently.

settings.title: Go lighter by day
settings.text: In humid heat, fresh and citrus scents feel easier; save rich ones for cool evenings.

settings.title: Mist your clothes too
settings.text: Fabric holds scent longer than skin in the heat (test on a hidden spot first).

settings.title: Keep it cool and dark
settings.text: Heat and sunlight spoil perfume: never leave a bottle in the car.
